status: Step 9: WAL file irreversibly lost after Step 4 checkpoint. All recovery attempts exhausted. Agent recognizes critical error but cannot proceed without environment reset or alternate data source. Task blocked.

knowledge.content: Task: Fix corrupted/encrypted WAL file in /app/ and extract all 11 records from SQLite database. Base database shows only 5 records, 6 more in WAL.
Required output: /app/recovered.json with format [{"id": 1, "name": "item1", "value": X}, ...] sorted by id. Must contain all 11 records.
Database location: /app/ directory. Database is in WAL (Write-Ahead Logging) mode.
WAL file issue: Appears corrupted or encrypted. SQLite cannot read it normally, showing only base data instead of all records.
Database files identified: /app/main.db (8.0K) and /app/main.db-wal (17K WAL file). The WAL file is unusually large compared to base database.
Table schema: 'items' table with columns (id, name, value). Base database contains 5 records: (1,'apple',100), (2,'banana',200), (3,'cherry',300), (4,'date',400), (5,'elderberry',500).

Critical: Running PRAGMA wal_checkpoint on a corrupted WAL file will DELETE it without recovery. The checkpoint operation in Step 4 permanently removed /app/main.db-wal (17KB) without applying any changes to main.db.

Critical realization: This is a challenge/puzzle task. The task description states "the WAL file appears to be corrupted or encrypted" and to "fix the WAL file so SQLite can read it." This implies the original WAL file (before checkpoint deletion) needed decryption/repair, not checkpointing. The solution requires examining the original WAL file bytes before any checkpoint operation.

procedural.content: Normal SQLite connection to /app/main.db shows only 5 records from base file, confirming WAL file is not being read/applied. WAL checkpoint not happening automatically.

WAL checkpoint attempt (PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(FULL)) returned (0, 0, 0) but still shows only 5 records. This indicates the WAL file is not being applied despite checkpoint command. The WAL file is likely corrupted at the binary level and needs direct inspection/repair.

Step 4 PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(FULL) returned (0,0,0) and permanently deleted the WAL file without merging data into main.db. The main.db modification timestamp remained Oct 24 2025 (unchanged), proving no data was written. This means checkpoint detected corrupted/invalid WAL and discarded it. The 6 additional records are lost unless WAL can be restored.

Steps 5-8: Extensive recovery attempts after WAL deletion all failed: no backups found in /app or /tmp, no .git version control, lsof shows no deleted file handles still open, filesystem-wide search found no copies of main.db-wal. The WAL file is permanently gone.

Fatal mistake in Step 4: Running PRAGMA wal_checkpoint on a corrupted/encrypted WAL file before examining its raw contents. The correct approach should have been: 1) Read raw WAL bytes first, 2) Identify corruption/encryption pattern, 3) Decrypt/fix the WAL file, 4) THEN checkpoint to merge data.

Step 9 checkpoint saved working context but no new recovery attempts made. Agent appears stuck in analysis loop after exhausting all technical recovery options (backups, version control, deleted handles, filesystem search). The fundamental blocker remains: WAL deleted before examining its bytes.
